title: Solar System
blurb: Planets, moons and our neighbourhood around the Sun

questions.question: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.fact: Mars gets its colour from iron oxide — basically rust — in its dusty soil.

questions.question: What is the largest planet in our Solar System?
questions.fact: Jupiter is so big that roughly 1,300 Earths could fit inside it.

questions.question: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.fact: A year on Mercury lasts just 88 Earth days.

questions.question: Which planet is famous for its spectacular ring system?
questions.fact: Saturn's rings are made mostly of chunks of water ice, from tiny grains to house-sized blocks.

questions.question: How many planets are there in our Solar System?
questions.fact: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet by the International Astronomical Union in 2006.

questions.question: Which is the hottest planet in the Solar System?
questions.fact: Venus's thick carbon-dioxide atmosphere traps heat, keeping its surface around 465 °C — hotter than Mercury.

questions.question: What kind of object is the Sun?
questions.fact: The Sun holds about 99.8% of all the mass in the Solar System.

questions.question: Which planet appears to rotate on its side, with an axial tilt of about 98°?
questions.fact: Scientists think a giant collision long ago knocked Uranus over onto its side.

questions.question: Olympus Mons, the tallest volcano in the Solar System, is found on which world?
questions.fact: Olympus Mons rises about 22 km — around two and a half times the height of Mount Everest.

questions.question: Which planet has the shortest day?
questions.fact: Jupiter spins once in just under 10 hours, despite being the largest planet.

questions.question: What is the largest moon in the Solar System?
questions.fact: Jupiter's moon Ganymede is even bigger than the planet Mercury.

questions.question: Which planet spins backwards (retrograde) compared with most others?
questions.fact: On Venus the Sun rises in the west — and a single day is longer than its year.

questions.question: The Great Red Spot is a giant storm on which planet?
questions.fact: The Great Red Spot has been observed for well over 150 years and is wider than Earth.

questions.question: The main asteroid belt lies between which two planets?
questions.fact: Despite the movies, asteroids in the belt are usually hundreds of thousands of kilometres apart.

questions.question: Roughly how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.fact: Light covers the ~150 million km from the Sun in about 8 minutes and 20 seconds.

questions.question: Which moon has a thick atmosphere and lakes of liquid methane?
questions.fact: Saturn's moon Titan is the only place besides Earth known to have stable liquid on its surface.

questions.question: What is the most volcanically active body in the Solar System?
questions.fact: Jupiter's moon Io has hundreds of active volcanoes, powered by tidal squeezing from Jupiter.

questions.question: What is the boundary where the Sun's solar wind meets interstellar space called?
questions.fact: Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause in 2012, becoming the first spacecraft in interstellar space.

questions.question: Which planet has the fastest winds ever measured in the Solar System?
questions.fact: Winds on Neptune can reach about 2,000 km/h — faster than the speed of sound on Earth.

questions.question: One Astronomical Unit (AU) is approximately…
questions.fact: 1 AU is the average Earth–Sun distance, about 149.6 million kilometres.

questions.question: Which dwarf planet is the largest object in the asteroid belt?
questions.fact: Ceres alone contains roughly a quarter of the asteroid belt's total mass.

questions.question: Which planet would float in a giant bathtub because its density is lower than water?
questions.fact: Saturn's average density is about 0.69 g/cm³ — less than water's 1 g/cm³.
